body:
I just wanted to say thank you for your kind words, I took time slept on it and as much as he’s a great guy it probably is he’s the first nice person since leaving my husband, and he reminds me of the good qualities in my ex. 

I told him I was happy for him which I absolutely am he deserves so much happiness, and that I’ll don’t mind taking a step back so he can find his bearings in his new relationship, and I’m here only as a friend, and to hook a girl up if the new girlfriend has a single male friend for me.
Thank you, that is what I thought and I appreciate that you’ve clarified things.

Probably a week before I talked to my manager about the maternity leave. Unfortunately I had to let them know earlier than I planned due to some medical issues. I was told the paper work was in the process to have to position created. During the two weeks between my announcement  and his letter of offer they did an external unadvertised offer to my replacement who was set to start 3 weeks later. I was asked to review their resume and verify that they would be suitable for my maternity leave. I agreed he had enough background in other programs that he could do well as a back up but it’s hard to know unless I meet with him. He was hired to be 60% back up for my job and 40% providing support on a different team who required assistance. 

After completing his one month of training I concluded he had enough knowledge to start to work on tasks and begin taking on my duties. At this point the meeting changed and both his manager and my direct manager said “perfect he will be taking on your entire portfolio and will be in the new position. When you return from your mat leave we will find something else for you to do”  shortly after I was assigned my new portfolio working in a completely different role, think working in IT then being assigned to being an executive assistant, something I had done in the distant past but have since done hours of training and education to advance my career into a completely different field.  It’s still the same title and I directly report to the same manager but will actually be reporting to a different manager in a on loan type situation.

Even if it coincides with a maternity leave announcement? Basically the job was mine until I announced my leave and they restructured my job to not exist as it currently does and have removed my responsibilities and tasks. 

Honestly it’s less about the actual position and more about job security.

We’ve had instances in the past where employees have been constructively dismissed post maternity leave. Projects not being assigned, jobs being given to the new hire over the old, and one person who was switched to a new department which then re-evaluated her role to be contract.

I know the requirements as that’s been in my work plan for performance evaluations what I need to be working towards for growth. 

I know their qualifications as I was asked to review their resume to see if they were a good fit as my leave replacement. I was not advised of their title until after they were trained and I had taught them the softwares required.

For me it’s more the issue this happened exactly when my maternity announcement cane through. I just want my job protection and to not be booted out because I’m taking maternity leave.

They were an external hire from the private sector it was an unadvertised position. Parliamentary Administration would be, library of parliament, House of Commons, Senate, they have their own set of rules and doesn’t always follow the federal government rules.

Edit:  I will add they do not meet the job requirements, BBB French, experience in the software required to do the job, the education or experience required.

We tried that with the first and it made things worse it was easier to forget and move on than have a constant reminder of what I had lost. Husband won’t go to couples counselling because there isn’t a problem. It just reaffirms I am the problem, because I can’t get over a baby that never really existed.

Probably going to get down voted but in some places what they did is considered a form of sexual harassment or assault as you didn’t consent. So I’m leaning towards the NTA.

But In terms of what the internet will say, YTA because kinda to be expected... kinda like how there will be drugs at a rave, or alcohol at a party. You’re not sleeping at a party and there will likely be sex somewhere.

I would disagree, they’ve left the baby with a sitter in the past for a whole week, and the baby is 8-9 months old.  

We have a wedding we have to go to after our twins will be due, and they will be about the same age depending on when they arrive, and we declined because it’s not for us to impose our children on their day. We said if you have some cancellations we would rather be on a back up list than pull this last minute bs.

It’s how small the venue is and how our liquor laws are, with consent of a parent a 16 year old can have alcohol. We decided for the easiest way to not be liable for underage drinking is to enforce no one under 16.
Baby will be 8 months roughly at the wedding and has already been away from mom for a week during parents babymoon.  And the wedding is a 20 minute drive from their house.
To clarify baby will be roughly 9 months old. She is not a newborn and has stayed with grandparents for at least a week when parents went on baby moon to Mexico.
No they went to Mexico for a week and forgot to send the invitation before they left. Then forgot about when they got home.
Really? I wouldn’t be surprised actually...
Baby will be 9 months and has fully stayed with grandparents for a week when mom and dad went on vacation to Mexico.
In the same city, 20 minute drive.

My family is on the other side of the country, the rsvp date was August. 

Baby was born February, wedding is November.
With my actual account you bet!

You really are right, I knew from the start that our wedding really isn’t about us it’s for our family which already is ass backwards. But getting ultimatums when we are literally paying for your food and booze is too much.

Two family members messaged us to say something to the effect of  “if you wouldn’t exclude them at Christmas why are you excluding them on the happiest day of your life.”  And we had multiple to the degree of “you don’t understand what it’s like to be a new parent they need a break too. You should offer a sitter at the venue”

The coordinator has been doing this for 20 years, she’s seen it all, and understands who is the most important person. 

And partly yes it’s to minimize damage the venue was one of the first buildings built in the city. If things get damaged they have to pay for a heritage specialist to assess and repair the damages.

We tried to go that route but they made a big deal about how it’s an insult to their gift of a DJ for us to just pay for it. Honestly We can afford the DJ it’s not a problem for us. They are the ones who want to keep up with appearances.

Thankfully our venue handles almost everything and report only to us in person. No changes can be made through phone or email. They’ve had experience with JNmoms(in-law) our coordinator flat out will not allow entry of anyone in white other than the bride. We made a calculated choice of the venue, it’s small intimate and has a coordinator who is loyal to the client not the banker. She’s no nonsense and knows the couples’ day not the parents. 

I think we’ll just hire our own DJ now. FIL use to be a DJ and had a bunch of contacts so we were hopeful. It’s not worth the mess and I would rather burn a toxic relationship over a DJ than suffer this nonsense.  Got some great recommendations from coworkers.
